[](https://news.ycombinator.com/vote?id=50150089&how=up&goto=item%3Fid%3D50150089)[I built a drone with only one motor [video]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ndftcft6XhU) ([youtube.com](https://news.ycombinator.com/from?site=youtube.com)) 24 points by [hakonjdjohnsen](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=hakonjdjohnsen)[1 hour ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50150089) | [hide](https://news.ycombinator.com/hide?id=50150089&goto=item%3Fid%3D50150089) | [past](https://hn.algolia.com/?query=I%20built%20a%20drone%20with%20only%20one%20motor&type=story&dateRange=all&sort=byDate&storyText=false&prefix&page=0) | [favorite](https://news.ycombinator.com/fave?id=50150089) | [3 comments](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50150089) [help](https://news.ycombinator.com/formatdoc) ![Image 2](https://news.ycombinator.com/s.gif)[](https://news.ycombinator.com/vote?id=50150780&how=up&goto=item%3Fid%3D50150089)[leoedin](https://news.ycombinator.com/user?id=leoedin)[10 minutes ago](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50150780) | [next](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50150089#50151284)[[–]](javascript:void(0)) A really neat concept. It uses a special hinge design, a magnetic encoder and torque modulation to control the lift of the rotor as it spins. Completely negates the need for a conventional helicopter's swash plate. The single motor does have the pretty major downside that it spins the moment it's in the air. I suspect a 2 motor drone with a tail motor would be a lot more practical. But I really like how mechanically simple the rotor hinge design is - it pushes all the complexity into the control algorithm. The only difference here is using a one-propeller drone.
